title: Air Zonk
subtitle: Bonk’s future takes flight
summary: Air Zonk is Red Company's cartoon shooter, released for TurboGrafx-16 in North America in October 1992.
body: Air Zonk is Red Company's cartoon shooter, released for TurboGrafx-16 in North America in October 1992. Zonk resembles Bonk, but sunglasses and cybernetic powers place this hero in a comic future. He flies through five scrolling stages against King Drool's machines, choosing a companion before the action begins. The resemblance connects the game to an established mascot while the constant flight supplies a different kind of adventure, built around shooting, charged attacks and the surprising shapes taken by Zonk's friends.

Collecting eight smiley faces summons the selected friend, who follows Zonk and adds supporting fire. Another set lets the pair merge into a hybrid with a new attack and a period of invulnerability. Each companion is available once, so choosing when to use a particular friend shapes the journey through the stages. The combinations make the cast part of the weapon system. A strange character encountered in the selection screen becomes a practical advantage whose movement and attack can change the next stretch of play.

Holding a shot charges an attack, while a longer charge produces a screen-wide bomb. Seven weapon power-ups provide further variations, each with a special charged form. Difficulty choices and friend settings let players adjust the challenge. Red Company developed the game with Naxat Soft, and Daisuke Morishima and Hisashi Matsushita composed its music. Air Zonk turns the familiar prehistoric world into a playful technological one, retaining its expressive creatures while making unlikely partnerships and transformations the center of the shooting.
story_headings: A companion becomes a new weapon
A mascot with a different attitude
